notes.summary: Independent current proof audit and reusable all-support canonical calculus; normal higher-dimensional CE remains unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs the canonical C/D raw-supremum identity, positivity before limits, all-degree convergence and FG implication. Rejudges the normal-surface, exact BFJ, conductor, cusp, crossing and gluing arguments at their full qualifications. Reads all actual/expanded current proofs and fourteen immediate primary units; historical recursive audit remains qualified.
notes.text:
The sole mathematical input is ENTIRE qualified G331, with its mandatory annotation, full source ledger and exact scope. The 422 actual FINAL fields, assembled notes, distinct expanded proofs, source/scope records, programs and compiler observations are DATA. This note reconstructs the envelope arguments used below and records the independent current audit. It does not grant historical or recursive reading credit.

Write C and D for G331's independently geometric continuous uniform cone and actual decreasing-C-net completion. Its positivity is actual negative effective finite REAL Cartier presentations on directed ACTUAL primary blowups, tested on EVERY contracted proper integral curve. Its proved comparison with ideal profiles is used; no ideal order completion is newly named geometric. All prime supports, quotient fraction-field evaluations, full normalization fibres, unit/zero/bottom cases and primary gauges remain present. Raw geometric and ideal cores need not coincide. Arbitrary-model cofinality, literal radial identification and an envelope theorem are not granted by G331.

Here is a reusable canonical lemma, proved independently. On compact X=V_a(R), for finite continuous signed f define A_0=R and A_m={g in R:v(g)+m f(v)>=0 for every v in X}. Ultrametricity makes these ideals, a power of a lies in each, and A_m A_n is contained in A_(m+n). If f is negative somewhere every A_m is proper primary; if f>=0 it is R. An integral-dependence equation has a uniquely least-valued leading term whenever a finite v(g) violates its bound, so A_m is integrally closed. Infinite values satisfy the tests already. The primary/unit profile h_m=-v(A_m)/m is continuous, finite and below f. On ACTUAL Bl_(A_m), its divisor -E_m/m is negative effective and relatively ample, with positive degree on EVERY contracted integral curve before any limiting statement. The unit case is zero.

The raw supremum p(f) over C minorants equals that over D minorants and equals sup_m h_m. Indeed G331 gives uniform rational primary/unit approximation in C. A small negative rational gauge correction retains the obstacle inequality; common denominators turn it into ideal multiplication. Any rational competitor -v(I)/r<=f has I contained in A_r. Conversely each h_m is a competitor. For g=inf_i g_i in D with g<=f, the increasing directed open sets {g_i<f+epsilon} cover X. Compactness gives one index valid throughout X; g_i-epsilon is a C minorant of f. Therefore g<=p(f)+epsilon; let epsilon decrease. This also handles partial bottom. The constant -max(0,-min f) supplies a finite lower barrier. No positivity or USC of p is presumed.

Let M_1=||v(A_1)|| and H_N=max_(1<=r<=N)h_r. If m=kr+s, 0<=s<r, grading gives h_m>=(kr/m)h_r-s M_1/m>=h_r-r M_1/m. Thus H_N-N M_1/m<=h_m<=p. Every degree converges pointwise to the finite lower semicontinuous p. Compact increasing strict-test covers show that p is continuous iff H_N converges uniformly, iff h_m converges uniformly. In that case p belongs to C and is the greatest C/D minorant. Negative gauge shifts prove ||p(f)-p(F)||<=||f-F||. Finite homogeneous generation forces continuity: if homogeneous generators g_j have degrees d_j, evaluation of every homogeneous monomial gives v(A_m)/m>=min_j v(g_j)/d_j; powers of the generators attain the infimum over m. Hence p=-v(J)/L, with L divisible by all d_j and J=(g_j^(L/d_j)). If f is negative somewhere J is proper; it is unit at each nonmaximal prime because A_1 is, so J is primary. This implication suffices for the non-FG deductions below. Non-FG alone is not a counterexample to CE.

Under a primary change b, d(v)=v(b) is bounded, positive and continuous, T(v)=v/d(v), and f_b(Tv)=f_a(v)/d(v). Each defining inequality divides by d(v), so canonical ideals are unchanged, and profiles and raw envelopes divide by d(v). Order bijections preserve existence/nonexistence of greatest minorants. G331's all-support completion homeomorphism and exact primary contraction transport the same lemma. A decreasing net of continuous obstacles having C envelopes has a greatest D envelope given by the actual decreasing net of their envelopes: every competitor is below each envelope. No increasing completion or arbitrary net flattening is used.

The normal-surface theorem was rejudged at its precise published domain. For an excellent NORMAL local DOMAIN of dimension TWO, normalize the blowup of a finite product of primary ideals including a. The result is a normal projective integral surface, regular off the closed fibre, with finite singular locus and normal singular local completions. These verify exactly condition (4) of Stacks 54.14.5. Its entire 54.14.3--5 proofs give a finite regular refinement by normalized blowups. The complete-normal-surface resolution, rational/double-point steps, completion transfer and gluing remain deeper published dependencies, not an independently recursive reconstruction.

Composition ampleness 29.38.7--8 combines negative tautological bundles into O(-E) ample for an effective exceptional E of full support. Normal proper birational 37.53.6 gives H0(Y,O)=R. This particular refinement is an ACTUAL primary blowup: finitely many affine nonvanishing section charts of powers of O(-E) cover Y; equalize degrees. The full 28.27.11 section-localization proof writes a finite set of affine algebra generators as t/s_i^k. In a common higher degree use s_i^K and t s_i^(K-k). Their ratios generate each affine chart, giving a projective closed immersion. The sections lie in R, generate an invertible ideal J O_Y, and J is proper primary since it is unit off the marked point. The immersion factors into integral Bl_J and contains its dense punctured open; its defining ideal is zero in that integral scheme. This proves the needed finite-list refinement, not general model cofinality.

On regular Y the exceptional prime curves E_i are actual effective Cartier. Put E_a=sum a_i E_i, a_i>0, D=sum d_i E_i, and Q_ij=deg_(E_i)O(E_j), over the marked residue field. Off-diagonal entries are nonnegative and symmetric by local effective intersection lengths. Every contracted integral curve is one of these curves. Feasible z satisfy z<=min(d,0), Qz>=0. A sufficiently negative -M a is feasible because O(-E_a) is generated. Coordinate maxima preserve feasibility: in a given row keep one input's diagonal coordinate and increase its nonnegative off-diagonal terms. In the compact box above the barrier, coordinate maximizers and their finite maximum give a greatest z*. Every feasible vector is dominated by one in that box after joining the barrier. Therefore Z*=sum z_i* E_i is actual negative effective REAL Cartier and curve-nef.

For any primary competitor -v(I)/s<=f_D, remove its exceptional divisorial part F_I. Normal height-one intersection puts every generator of I in H0(Y,O(-F_I)). On EACH exceptional CURVE some generator has nonzero generic restriction after removal, so its line-bundle degree is nonnegative. Thus -F_I/s is feasible and <=Z*. For any support p, the valuation ring of Frac(R/p) has its proper centre on Y and a generic point off the fibre. Pull back the exceptional invertible lattice with that generic trivialization. Regular generator ratios give -v(I)/s<=f_(-F_I/s)<=f_(Z*) even if some generators are killed. The canonical lemma proves p(f_D)=f_(Z*). Signed primary differences form a separating lattice, with min(vI-vJ,vK-vH)=v(IH+KJ)-v(JH); (g)+a^N separates all supports and a gives constants. Compact lattice approximation and the Lipschitz bound therefore prove CE for ALL continuous signed obstacles on these normal surfaces, over arbitrary residue fields and in equal or mixed characteristic. No finite generation or rate follows.

The independent BFJ application remains ONLY at a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. For a signed model F fixed by a retraction, the max-directed nef coefficients below F, with a negative barrier, have bounded weak-nef supremum W. BFJ 3.11 supplies substantive CLOSED-simplex continuity; the extension is the infimum over ALL retractions. Divisorial bounds, continuity on simplices and refining the fixed model put H_W below F on all supports. G331's exact BFJ D comparison bounds every competitor by H_W. Canonical ideals are L-infinity(mW); truncating (g)+mhat^N with N>=m max(0,-min F) passes divisorial tests to all supports, and G331 contracts the primary ideals. For W nonzero, 3.14 gives strict negativity; fixed-complex thinness gives A_thin<=-CW. The WHOLE 3.18 proof works for real t>C; use t=m+C to obtain (1+C/m)W<=W_m<=W and consequently 0<=H_W-h_m<=C max(0,-min F)/m on EVERY support by closed-simplex continuity and all-retraction infima. Uniform model density and Lipschitz give smooth CE at these hypotheses. Zero uses the unit ideal; bottom is separate; DVR and empty cases are direct. Higher-dimensional positive/mixed-characteristic source CE is not inferred.

The current conductor arguments were independently checked. If the FULL reduced conductor-quotient boundary restriction is injective, G331's finite singleton stratum and infinite quotient-fibre rule make normalization boundary restriction a homeomorphism, with positive order/isometric C/D descent. Envelopes transport and CE is equivalent on the normal centres. Primary conductors suffice. Finite radicial reduced quotients suffice too: a support has its unique support prime and purely inseparable quotient field extension, forcing w(t)=v(t^(p^e))/p^e. No perfection or uniform exponent is needed. Canonical ideals contract; extension equality or inherited rates are not claimed.

For a numerical-semigroup ring k[t^H,z]_0 with conductor exponent c, normalization is k[t,z]_0 and conductor t^c S. A coefficient at exponent h<c cannot be conductor: multiplication by t^(c-1-h) exposes the forbidden exponent c-1. Localization preserves this finite-module conductor. Reduced quotients are the same z-ring, so transport gives CE in the BFJ smooth range in every dimension and on normal surfaces over every field. The mixed cusp over Z_p has the same reduced quotient and normal surface source. For H=<2,3>, b=z_1+t and A=w((b,t^2,z_2,...)), the actual primary K_m=(b^m(z_1-mt),t^2 b^m,t^(2m+2))+(z_2,...)^m has no t-linear term in any characteristic. With s=w(t),u=w(z_1),B=w(b),U=min_(j>=2)w(z_j), min(2s,u,U)=1, A=min(B,2s,U), all generators have value>=mA. If U=A there is equality. Otherwise, 2s<=B forces s=u=1 and the last generator gives mA+2; B<2s and s<=u gives s<=1 and the second gives mA+2s; s>u gives B=w(z_1-mt)=u=1 and the first gives mA+1, even when m=0 in k. Thus the all-support error is at most 2/m. In characteristic zero, valuations killing t with z_1=1 and monomial (t,b) weights (1,2) give A=1,2. A primary generator attaining z-order e has a nonzero z^e coefficient and no t-linear term, so its degree-e part cannot be a scalar b^e; after z=b-t some t^(e-j)b^j, j<e, survives with weight<=2e-1. Different total degrees cannot cancel it. Every nonzero finite REAL positive primary combination has strict ratio<2, while A has ratio2. This proves CE without raw attainment and without FG, not CE failure.

The retained threefold example remains a diagnostic: blow up the regular origin and two rational exceptional points P,Q. For I=(z)+m^2, the x-chart is x(w,x), hence its divisorial part is E_1+2E_2+2E_3. Its negative restriction on E_1=Bl_(P,Q)P^2 is H-e_P-e_Q and the joining line has degree -1; the other exceptional planes have degree1. The same ample-section/Rees argument makes this model actual primary. A generic section on an exceptional SURFACE does not imply all-curve-nefness. The genuine primary profile remains geometric on its own blowup. This is not normal CE failure.

For current 422/420 crossings, direct factoring through the killed component and coefficient-order comparison prove that all competitors on the second branch are bounded by its generic order value. For 0<a<b, the compatible obstacle -a on branch1 and -a-(b-a)/w(y) on branch2 has canonical ideal m^ceil(mb)+x m^(ceil(ma)-1), raw p=-a at finite-x branch1 and -b elsewhere, and exact uniform gap ceil(mb)/m-a. The signed model (1/2)v((y)+m^2)-(3/2)v(m) has the same half-gap filtration. Effective negative primary divisors are ample before the limit. Monomial x=r,z_j=1 converges to a conductor point and proves non-USC, no greatest C/D minorant, and failure of positivity of USC regularization. Perturbation less than 1/4 preserves the half-gap contradiction. These checked inherited results are not presented as new progress.

For regular normal SURFACE centres glued along the SAME marked DVR with principal nonzero kernels and common quotient gauge, normal CE gives H_i. Set a=min H_i(o_i). Zero dichotomy gives either all H_i=0 if a=0, or C barriers B_i<=H_i with B_i(o_i)=a by scaling negative H_i, using constant a on a zero branch. For N>=n||H_i-B_i||, max(B_i,H_i-w(x_i)/n)=max(B_i,H_i-w((x_i)+a_i^N)/n) is C and equals a at o_i. Actual primary truncation, cone maxima/addition and full-fibre positive descent make a target minorant reaching H_i off the conductor. Hence raw p equals H_i there and a at the shared point; equality of every H_i(o_i) is necessary and sufficient for greatest C/D existence. An unequal value contradicts USC along a finite-kernel-value dense net. This proof requires distinct normalization centres; it does not assume independent product factors when they are absent. For completeness the inherited cross-component necessity follows directly: use regular conductor c_0 and normalization idempotents e_1,e_2, so j=c_0e_1 and ell=c_0e_2 are actual R-elements. At a fibre alpha,beta on these components, the normal bound gives g(beta)<=g(nu)/K. Choose L>nu(ell), B with D_0=1+B(1-nu(ell)/L)>K. The signed obstacle (B/L)v((ell)+a^L)-(B+1) is -1 on component1, but every minorant has value<=-D_0/K<-1 at the fibre. Actual primary a^((B+1)n)+(j)a^n has profile reaching -1 on the dense finite-j first-component locus and equal -(B+1) on the other components. USC at alpha is impossible for a greatest minorant. If dim R/(p_1+p_2)>0, a valuation of this quotient lifts into the two minimal normalization factors, giving that fibre. Thus for excellent reduced local dimension<=2 with NORMAL component rings, universal CE iff every pairwise intersection is zero-dimensional: sufficiency is uniqueness of the component at every support below m and normal-surface/DVR transport. This classification does not include irreducible nonnormal rings.

Finally, on reduced curve links the normalization centres are DVRs and conductor values are finite. There are no conductor identifications on the finite branch set. Positive descent gives all nonpositive functions and envelope min(f,0). Literal classical/CLD logarithmic radial extension is a different class, retaining its mixed-zero obstruction. Nilpotents are invisible and dimension-zero reduction has empty boundary. Products, energy and full finite operators are separate targets.

Evidence and audit boundary: all five actual settled FINAL notes, every one of their five fields, and all five distinct expanded proofs were physically read in untruncated bounded outputs. Their parsed actual fields were checked against the settled FINAL file; the assembled-note version is distinct and is retained separately. The unique current preamble/abstract, complete current scope records, ledger, verdict, unchanged residual and entire 420 proof were read. The three supplied native programs were read only as inert DATA. Artifact n1.md records this argument; all exact current bodies remain in proof-companion.md and retained/. notes.summary: Distinct MARKED normalization centres obstruct geometric envelopes, even for DOMAIN normalization.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves the CRT/conductor proposal on every support with actual primary-model obstacles and all-curve-positive competitors. Requires a full fibre joining distinct closed normal centres, not distinct minimal components. Gives a positive canonical uniform gap in every degree and stable perturbation failure. Same-centre fibres are not decided.
notes.text:
Marked-centre obstruction, proved relative to ENTIRE qualified G331 and n1. Let R be excellent reduced local of positive dimension, a a proper primary gauge, S its finite normalization, and rho the FULL normalized boundary quotient. Write M_1,...,M_q for S's finitely many closed centres over m and S_i=S_(M_i), using the appropriate normal-domain factor of S. If one rho-fibre contains alpha on centre M_1 and beta on a DISTINCT centre M_2, there is a bounded strictly negative continuous signed PRIMARY-MODEL obstacle with neither a greatest geometric C nor a greatest geometric D minorant. S may be a DOMAIN; distinct minimal components are not required. No source CE or higher-dimensional resolution is assumed.

The local primary gauge a_i=a S_i has M_i^r_i contained in a_i for some integer r_i>=1. Every normalized w on that centre has w(M_i)>=1/r_i. Denominators outside M_i are units and have value0, so these inequalities hold on ALL source supports, and w(a)=w(a_i)=1. Chinese remainder gives h in S with h=1 modulo M_1 and h=0 modulo EVERY other M_i, and k in S with k=0 modulo M_1 and k=1 modulo M_2. At M_1, h is a unit; elsewhere it is a nonunit. At M_2, k is a unit. These are elements of the finite semilocal normalization, not falsely asserted downstairs units or idempotents.

Choose a regular c_0 in the conductor c=(R:S). Since c is an S-ideal, c_0 times EVERY element of S lies in R. A nontrivial fibre is conductor-infinite by G331, so alpha and beta kill c_0. The conductor is proper and c_0 is a nonunit of R; hence it is positive and nonzero on every generic centred source valuation. On M_2 choose a normalized centred divisorial nu, available by G331 divisorial density. Its normal-domain order bound gives finite K>=1 such that nu(I)<=K beta(I) for EVERY unit-or-primary ideal of S_2. More explicitly, after normalizing nu, nu(f)<=C_nu ord_(M_2)(f) for nonzero nonunits and beta(M_2)>=1/r_2. Choose a generator attaining the primary ideal's finite beta-value. Then nu(I)<=C_nu r_2 beta(I); units are zero. Uniform comparison and actual decreasing infima consequently give g(rho beta)<=g(rho nu)/K for EVERY target geometric C or D function, including bottom. This bound is applied to the excellent NORMAL local domain S_2; no analytic irreducibility of nonnormal R is asserted.

Put d=nu(c_0)>0. Choose integers L>d and B>0 with D_0=1+B(1-d/L)>K; write b=B+1. Choose an integer M>=L r_1 and set ell=c_0 k^M, an ACTUAL element of R. On EVERY point of centre M_1, w(ell)>=M/r_1>=L, while nu(ell)=d since k is a unit at M_2. The ideal I=(ell)+a^L is proper primary: it contains a^L and ell cannot be a unit of R since its M_1 value is positive. Define F=(B/L)v(I)-b v(a). On V_a, F lies in [-b,-1], is exactly -1 on the ENTIRE M_1 boundary image and at the common fibre, and F(rho nu)=-D_0<-K. Primary evaluations prove continuity on every support. It is a signed exceptional REAL Cartier evaluation on a directed common ACTUAL primary blowup of I and a.

For each n>=1 choose an integer M_n>=B n max_(i!=1)r_i. Put j_n=c_0 h^(M_n) in R, T_n=a^(bn)+(j_n)a^n and q_n=-v(T_n)/n. T_n is ACTUAL proper primary. On its actual blowup, -E_(T_n)/n is negative effective and relatively ample, so has positive degree on EVERY contracted proper integral curve BEFORE any limit. On M_1 its exact profile is max(-b,-1-w(c_0)/n), since h is a unit there. At every other centre, w(j_n)>=M_n/r_i>=Bn, so q_n=-b. These formulas include infinite c_0-values and all nonminimal supports. Thus q_n<=F EVERYWHERE. On the M_1 finite-c_0 locus, sup_n q_n=-1. That locus is dense by G331's all-support divisorial density: c_0 is nonzero in S_1, so every generic-support centred divisorial point has finite c_0-value. In particular alpha is in its closure. A convergent NET suffices; no metrizability is used.

Every C/D minorant g<=F has g(rho beta)<=-D_0/K<-1. If there were a greatest minorant, it would dominate all q_n and equal -1 on the dense finite-c_0 M_1 locus, because F=-1 there. Its normalization pullback is USC. A strict sublevel neighbourhood of alpha at the forced value below -1 would meet that dense locus, a contradiction. Therefore neither greatest minorant exists. Equivalently the raw supremum p is -1 on that locus and <=-D_0/K at the common point, so p is not USC. This proves the proposed CRT route, including actual ring membership, uniform centre bounds, proper primary models and every-support positivity.

There are quantitative consequences. Set eta=D_0/K-1>0. Each canonical h_m of n1 is continuous and <=p. At alpha it is <=-D_0/K; its values on a finite-c_0 M_1 net approaching alpha tend to that value, whereas p on that net is -1. Therefore ||p-h_m||>=eta in EVERY degree. The canonical algebra is not finitely generated by n1's proved implication. No exact formula for the whole raw p away from this locus and this fibre is claimed. Failure is stable for ||F'-F||<epsilon<(D_0-K)/(K+1): q_n-epsilon are C minorants of F', forcing a greatest minorant to be >=-1-epsilon on the dense locus, while the normal bound forces its common-fibre value <=(-D_0+epsilon)/K<-1-epsilon. All functions are homogeneous on rays; primary changes divide by the same bounded positive denominator, preserve nonexistence and transform the canonical ideals exactly.

An algebraic sufficient condition is that c has a quotient-boundary fibre whose lifts lie in two distinct marked centres. In particular positive-dimensional intersections of distinct minimal components give such fibres: a valuation of the positive-dimensional quotient R/(p_1+p_2) lifts separately through the two finite normalizations. This recovers the previous crossing result as a special case rather than restating it as new mathematics. Universal CE implies that EVERY normalization fibre stays within ONE marked centre. This necessary condition does not assert that such a fibre must be singleton. Irreducible excellent domains whose normalization has several marked centres are covered whenever a full conductor fibre connects them; mere existence of several centres, without such a fibre, is insufficient. Curves remain consistent: their conductor quotient has empty centred boundary.

Same-marked-centre fibres, general NORMAL dimension>=3 CE, products, energy and full finite operators are not solved by this theorem. All model/source/audit/radial qualifications of G331 remain. Artifact n2.md contains the universal proof; n2.tex is its expanded delivery form. Rerun: python assemble.py; python verify_delivery.py. Finite arithmetic is diagnostic, not certification of this theorem.

notes.summary: Irreducible self-crossing has no greatest C/D minorant; exact canonical error is ceil(3m/2)/m-1.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves domain normalization, exact conductor/quotients, signed primary obstacle, full raw envelope and every-degree canonical ideals over char!=2 fields in all dimensions>=2 and excellent DVR surfaces with2 invertible. Every primary divisor is actually ample before limits. Failure is nonnormal, not a normal CE counterexample.
notes.text:
An irreducible self-crossing example, with exact canonical ideals in EVERY degree. Use ENTIRE qualified G331 and n1--n2. Let k be ANY field with char(k)!=2 and d>=2, let z=(z_1,...,z_(d-1)), and
R=k[u,v,z]_(u,v,z)/(v^2-u^2(1+u)), m=(u,v,z).
This is an excellent DOMAIN of dimension d. The element 1+u is not a square in k(u,z), since its prime divisor has odd order. Thus the displayed quadratic is irreducible; its parametrization u=t^2-1, v=t(t^2-1) embeds R in its fraction field. Write S_0=k[t,z]. It is normal, finite over the unlocalized R_0 via integral t with t^2=1+u, and has the same fraction field since t=v/u. Hence it is the normalization. Localizing at R_0\m gives a NORMAL DOMAIN S with exactly two closed centres M_+=(t-1,z), M_-=(t+1,z). It is the semilocalization of k[t,z] at these centres: every element outside their union is a unit in the finite algebra over local R, proving the identification with that semilocalization. S is not a product of two rings.

All conductor claims are exact. Put A=k[u,z]. Then S_0=A direct-sum tA as A-module and R_0=A direct-sum tuA. For a+t b in S_0, membership in R_0 forces b in uA; multiplication by t then forces a in uA as well. Conversely uS_0 multiplies S_0 into R_0. Thus the conductor is uS_0 before localization and uS afterwards, since the conductor is the annihilator of the finite module S_0/R_0 and annihilators of finite modules localize. Its target ideal is (u,v). The quotient is R/c=k[z]_(z), while S/c is TWO copies of that ring, because t^2-1=(t-1)(t+1) with coprime factors. Exactly R=k[z]_(z)+uS: subtract the lifted quotient residue, leaving uS. This is a conductor fibre product, not a decomposition of the normalization domain. Moreover mS=(u,z); on either normal local centre this is its maximal ideal since the opposite t-sign factor is a unit.

Consequently every normalized target semivaluation has its source lift(s) on these two centres. The finite-u stratum has unique lifts. At infinite u-value, the ENTIRE quotient-boundary semivaluation on k[z] has two lifts, one at each centre, and these are exactly the identifications by G331. For d=2 it is one conductor point o with z_1=1; for d>2 it retains every support of the z-quotient. This proves the marked-centre hypothesis of n2 in an irreducible nonnormal ring.

There is a fully explicit obstacle requiring no unknown Izumi constant. Let ell=v-u=u(t-1) in R, I=(ell)+m^2, and F=(1/2)v(I)-2v(m). This is a continuous signed ACTUAL primary-model evaluation. On the plus centre, put s=w(t-1), Z=min_j w(z_j), so min(s,Z)=1 and w(u)=s; t+1 is a unit. Then w(ell)=2s>=2, hence F=-1 on its ENTIRE boundary. On the minus centre put r=w(t+1), with min(r,Z)=1, and t-1 a unit. There w(ell)=r and F=(1/2)min(r,2)-2, between -3/2 and -1. All conductor values are -1. These identities hold when coordinates are infinite; ideal I is proper primary and its evaluations are finite.

The generic ordinary-order valuation nu_- on the regular local minus centre has r=Z=1 and F(nu_-)=-3/2. Every normalized semivaluation on that centre dominates ordinary order: all regular parameters have value>=1, every element of the e-th maximal power has value>=e, and units have value0. Thus for every unit-or-primary target ideal w(J)>=nu_-(J). Negative REAL combinations, G331 uniform comparison and ACTUAL decreasing infima give g(rho w)<=g(rho nu_-) for EVERY target geometric C/D function on the entire minus image, including all conductor supports. Every minorant of F is therefore <=-3/2 there.

For n>=1 define the ACTUAL conductor element j_n=u(t+1)^(n-1) in R and the proper primary ideal T_n=m^(3n)+(j_n)m^(2n), with q_n=-v(T_n)/(2n). On the plus centre, w(j_n)=s, so q_n=max(-3/2,-1-s/(2n)). On the minus centre, w(j_n)=nr>=n, so q_n=-3/2. They are <=F on every source and target support. The negative effective primary divisors -E_(T_n)/(2n) are relatively ample and positive on EVERY contracted integral curve before any limit. The constant -3/2 is also a competitor. Hence the COMPLETE raw C/D supremum is
p=-1 on the plus-centre finite-u locus, and p=-3/2 on the entire minus image, including every conductor point.
No generic-support restriction is present in this formula.

At the plus centre the monomial valuations w_R(t-1)=R, w_R(z_j)=1, R->infinity, converge pointwise on every element of its polynomial local ring to the valuation killing t-1 and having ordinary z-order. Every fixed unit denominator has value0. Their target restrictions converge to a conductor point, where the raw value drops by 1/2. Thus p is not USC and neither a greatest C nor a greatest D minorant exists. This is NONNORMAL failure on an irreducible germ, not normal CE failure. Its USC regularization has value -1 at that conductor point and -3/2 at nu_-: the open test v(ell)<2 around nu_- meets only the minus image. It violates g(o)<=g(nu_-), so regularization does not restore geometric positivity.

The canonical filtration has an exact finite algebraic description. For EVERY integer m>=1 put c_m=ceil(3m/2), and in S put
J_m=(t-1,z)^(m-1)(t+1,z)^(c_m-1).
The two semilocal ideals are comaximal since 2 is invertible; their product equals their intersection. Then
A_m(F)=(z)^(c_m) R + u J_m,
where uJ_m is contained in R by the conductor. This is a genuine R-ideal with explicit finite generators: all z-monomials of total degree c_m, and u t^epsilon times every product of a degree-(m-1) monomial in (t-1,z) and a degree-(c_m-1) monomial in (t+1,z), for epsilon=0,1. S=R+Rt, so these generators span exactly uJ_m over R. Each polynomial is an actual downstairs element; use t^2=1+u and ut=v to write it in u,v,z.

Proof of the identity: testing ordinary order at the plus and minus centres forces respectively order>=m and order>=c_m. Those conditions suffice on EVERY source support because normalized values dominate order and F is respectively -1 and >=-3/2. Every f in R has a decomposition f=g(z)+u a, with g in the local z-ring and a in S. The minus order condition forces g in (z)^(c_m), by reducing modulo u; the quotient regular local ring has its usual power filtration. Subtract this residue lift. Since u is a regular parameter on BOTH normal centres, the remaining u a has the required orders exactly when a is in the localized (m-1)-st plus power and (c_m-1)-st minus power. In a semilocal ring these local conditions are their intersection, equal to J_m. Conversely the displayed ideal satisfies both conditions. This argument includes localized unit denominators and all cancellation; it is not an inferred monomial filtration.

Upon localization at the plus centre, the other centre's power is the unit ideal. Thus on EVERY plus support
h_m=-min(c_m Z,s+m-1)/m.
At every minus support, including conductor supports, h_m=-c_m/m. Every h_m has the ACTUAL negative effective ample primary presentation from n1. These formulas prove pointwise convergence in EVERY degree to p. The EXACT uniform error is
||p-h_m||=c_m/m-1 >=1/2.
Indeed on the plus finite-u locus the gap is at most c_m/m-1, attained by Z=1 and finite s>=c_m-m+1. On the minus image it is c_m/m-3/2, which is 0 in even degree and 1/(2m) in odd degree. Therefore the largest gap is 1/2 in even degree and 1/2+1/(2m) in odd degree. The canonical algebra is not finitely generated by n1's proved forward implication. Failure persists for uniform perturbations <1/4 by q_n-epsilon and the same ordinary-order inequality.

The same construction works in every dimension d>=2 over every field of characteristic different from2, as proved above. It also works for the genuinely mixed-characteristic irreducible SURFACE R=V[u,v]_(pi,u,v)/(v^2-u^2(1+u)), for any excellent DVR V with 2 invertible. Its normalization is the semilocal domain V[t] at (pi,t-1),(pi,t+1), the conductor is uS, the quotients are V and V times V, and mS=(pi,u). The same free rank-two module calculation proves normalization and conductor; irreducibility follows over Frac(V)(u), and regularity/normality of V[t] supplies the source. Replace z by pi throughout. Ordinary (pi,t+1)-order is a valuation since its associated graded ring is a polynomial domain, and every normalized support dominates it. The same explicit F,T_n,A_m,h_m,p and exact gap formulas hold. No claim is made when2 is not invertible. The characteristic-two displayed field equation degenerates and is not an automatic transfer of this example.

All expressions are homogeneous on rays. Under a transported primary obstacle the canonical ideals are unchanged and profiles and p divide by the bounded positive gauge factor; greatest-minorant failure is gauge invariant. Completion transport holds, although the irreducible nonnormal ring need not have a domain completion. No analytic irreducibility assertion is made for R. notes.text:
Exact irreducible surface criterion and a same-centre boundary/barrier theorem. Use ENTIRE qualified G331 and n1--n3. These deductions do not assert that every nonsingleton fibre obstructs envelopes.

First, for the self-crossing SURFACE in n3 over any field of characteristic different from2, or its excellent DVR version with2 invertible, EVERY finite continuous signed obstacle f has the following exact rule. The normalization S is a semilocal DOMAIN with two regular normal SURFACE centres. Its boundary is the DISJOINT union of the two local-centre boundaries, and its C/D classes are their products by G331; disconnected boundary pieces do not require algebraic component idempotents in S. Let f_+,f_- be the source restrictions, H_+,H_- their continuous geometric envelopes, existing by the normal-surface proof in n1. The conductor quotient is the marked DVR k[z]_(z), or V, so the only nontrivial boundary fibre is o_+,o_- over o. Set a=min(H_+(o_+),H_-(o_-)). Then
p(rho w)=H_i(w) when w(u)<infinity on centre i, and p(o)=a.
A greatest geometric C or D minorant exists iff H_+(o_+)=H_-(o_-). When it exists it is continuous and belongs to C. This is an obstacle-by-obstacle NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT condition on an irreducible nonnormal germ, not solely the explicit counterexample.

Here is the positive lower bound without pretending a fibrewise minimum is psh. If a=0, G331's normal zero dichotomy gives both H_i=0, so zero descends and is the envelope. If a<0 and H_i(o_i)<0, set B_i=(a/H_i(o_i))H_i; the ratio is >=1 and B_i<=H_i. If H_i(o_i)=0, normal zero dichotomy gives H_i=0 and use constant B_i=a. These are C functions with B_i(o_i)=a. For n>=1 and an integer N>=max(1,n||H_i-B_i||), define
G_(i,n)=max(B_i,H_i-w(u)/n), interpreting the second term as bottom where u is killed.
Exactly G_(i,n)=max(B_i,H_i-w((u)+a_i^N)/n). The ideal term is ACTUAL primary, with a negative effective relatively ample divisor positive on EVERY contracted integral curve; G331 addition, scaling and maxima prove membership in C, not merely pointwise nonpositivity. Equality follows since H_i-N/n<=B_i. The tuple has common conductor value a and is fibre constant everywhere, since all other fibres are singletons. G331 full-fibre POSITIVE descent gives a target C minorant of f. Its increasing pointwise limit equals H_i at finite-u points and retains a at o. Increasing-limit closure is not invoked: these are lower bounds for the raw supremum. Every target D competitor pulls back below H_i and has a common value<=both H_i(o_i), proving the upper bound.

If the values agree, the tuple H_i itself descends positively to the continuous greatest envelope. If H_i(o_i)>a for some i, the finite-u locus is dense by divisorial density (u is nonzero), and continuity of H_i makes its values along a net to o_i converge to the larger value. The computed p is not USC. A greatest C/D minorant would equal p and hence cannot exist. This proof also applies whenever an excellent reduced local surface has finite normalization with regular SURFACE local centres, FULL infinite-conductor boundary consisting of one lift per centre over a single target point, and a nonzero conductor element u whose killed locus on each centre is just that point. The stated full-fibre and local cone hypotheses are necessary to this application; there is no arbitrary conductor minimum theorem.

Next consider the pinch family, independently computing its entire relevant normalization data. For ANY field k put
R=k[t^2,ty,y,s]_(t^2,ty,y,s), S=k[t,y,s]_(t,y,s).
This is a DOMAIN with presentation k[u,x,y,s]_(u,x,y,s)/(x^2-u y^2), u=t^2,x=ty. The quadratic is irreducible since u is not a square in k(u,y,s), including in characteristic2; alternatively the displayed subring embedding and rank-two normal form prove the presentation. The integral element t satisfies t^2=u and lies in the fraction field as x/y. Thus S is finite, normal and birational, hence the normalization. Its UNIQUE marked centre is the origin: t^2,y,s vanish only there above the target maximal ideal. With A=k[u,y,s], S_0=A direct-sum tA and R_0=A direct-sum tyA. Membership of a+tb in R_0 requires b divisible by y, and multiplying by t requires a divisible by y. Hence the conductor is exactly yS, which as an R-ideal is (y,x). The annihilator calculation localizes exactly. Its quotient map is
k[u,s]_(u,s) -> k[t,s]_(t,s), u -> t^2.
The target maximal primary gauge a=(u,x,y,s) extends to (t^2,y,s). These computations retain all source and quotient supports.

When char(k)!=2 there is an EXACT two-point FULL boundary fibre inside this ONE marked normal centre. Let alpha have support (y,t-s), beta have support (y,t+s), and give s value1 on their k[s] quotients. Both have w(aS)=min(2, infinity,1)=1, both kill the conductor, and their target restriction has support (x,y,u-s^2), with u-value2 and s-value1. The restrictions agree on EVERY element of R, since x,y are killed and t^2=s^2 in either quotient; every local unit has value0. They are distinct, since alpha(t-s)=infinity while beta(t-s)=1. The fibre has exactly these two points: modulo that target support the integral equation becomes t^2=s^2, with exactly the two primes t=±s; their quotient fraction fields are k(s), on which the given base valuation has its unique identical extension. Both centres remain the same maximal ideal (t,y,s). Thus this example is a concrete remaining same-centre conductor fibre, not an instance of n2.

Without the extra parameter s the pinch SURFACE R=k[t^2,ty,y]_(t^2,ty,y) has conductor yS and quotient map k[u]_(u)->k[t]_(t). Each quotient centred boundary is a singleton. Normalization restriction is therefore bijective on the FULL boundary, using G331 finite-conductor uniqueness elsewhere. At the conductor source point w(t)=1/2,w(y)=infinity for the extended gauge (t^2,y), giving target u-value1. Positive order/isometric transport and n1's arbitrary-field normal-SURFACE CE prove continuous geometric envelopes for ALL continuous signed obstacles on this irreducible nonnormal pinch surface, over EVERY field. This is a positive example with a nonprimary conductor and a separable degree-two conductor quotient when char(k)!=2. There is no assertion that its algebraic quotient map is radicial in that characteristic.

In characteristic2 the threefold quotient k[u,s]->k[t,s] is finite radicial. Directly, every polynomial in t,s has square in k[u,s] without assuming k perfect, so its valuation is forced to be half the value of that square; the same holds for quotient fields and every support. The full normalization boundary map is bijective. Thus CE is equivalent to the normal-source CE, with no new arbitrary-characteristic threefold CE conclusion. The char(k)!=2 two-point fibre is not asserted in characteristic2.

There is a quantitative same-centre obstruction to the proposed METHOD, distinct from an envelope counterexample. On ANY excellent NORMAL local centre A with primary gauge a, choose a normalized centred divisorial nu. G331's normal bound supplies K_nu>=1, independent of w, with nu(I)<=K_nu w(I) for every unit-or-primary ideal and EVERY normalized w on that SAME centre. Indeed nu(f)<=C ord_m(f), m^r contained in a, and w(m)>=1/r give K_nu=C r after adjusting normalization; units are zero. Thus every geometric C/D function obeys g(w)<=g(nu)/K_nu throughout the centre. If an obstacle F satisfies F(nu)=-D with D>K_nu, EVERY minorant, and hence its raw supremum, is <=-D/K_nu<-1 EVERYWHERE on that centre. Competitors cannot approach -1 on even a dense subset there. More specifically, if a proposed j_n has nu(j_n)>=c n, then w(j_n)/n>=c/K_nu for EVERY w, so max(-b,-1-w(j_n)/n)<=max(-b,-1-c/K_nu)<-1 whenever b>1. Powers of a nonunit cannot create a downstairs separator shallow on one region and uniformly deep at a fixed divisorial point in the same marked centre. A local element is either a unit at all centred valuations or a nonunit at all; there are no CRT units separating these lifts. This proves why n2's separate-centre construction cannot simply be reused at alpha,beta in the pinch threefold.

A useful general NORMAL/higher-dimensional deduction follows without CE. If a finite continuous signed obstacle f on an excellent normal local domain is negative anywhere, continuity and divisorial density give a centred divisorial nu with f(nu)<0. The preceding uniform K_nu bound gives
-max(0,-min f) <= p(f)(w) <= f(nu)/K_nu <0 for EVERY support w.
If f>=0, p(f)=0. Thus even the raw supremum has a uniform strict-negative bound in the nonzero case. The same conclusion holds for an excellent nonnormal germ whose finite normalization has a SINGLE marked normal local centre: pull f and every competitor to that centre. This includes the same-centre pinch test. It proves boundedness and excludes mixed-zero raw patterns; it does not prove USC, continuity, actual D attainment or greatest-minorant existence.

Finally, if source continuous envelopes are known and the source envelope of a particular pulled-back obstacle is constant on EVERY normalization fibre, G331 positive descent proves a continuous target envelope. Every target competitor pulls back below it, and its compatible descent is itself a competitor. This is a sufficient criterion in the pinch threefold with smooth algebraically closed characteristic-zero source, using n1's exact BFJ CE; necessity is not asserted there. Same-centre nonsingleton-fibre CE/appropriate envelope classification and general excellent NORMAL dimension>=3 CE or qualifying failure remain OPEN.
